edits.add_before: | `ops-review-round-2/*.json` | Spent 2026-08-24, `--no-approval` disclosed (repairs the commits it reviews). **Second adversarial review: 5 High, 4 Medium, 8 Low, all confirmed by execution — and the High findings are in the FIX for round 1.** Round 1 gated the file-guard allowlist on the file's EXTENSION; `classify()` returns on the first match, so every `.key`/`.pem` reached the certificate branch before the k8s/PII/api-token/ssh branches could claim it. `k8s/tests/secret-tls.key`, `tests/api_key.key`, `pii/tests/customers.key` and `tests/fixtures/.ssh/deploy.key` were all still clean. "Unreachable for any other extension" was true and irrelevant — the same sentence the round-1 reviewer had written about round-1's claim. Fix: the allowlist left `classify()` entirely and is applied to the VERDICT, only when no stronger category fires, only when stripping the certificate suffix reveals nothing stronger, and never under `k8s/`/`pii/`/`production/`/`secrets/`/`credentials/`/`.ssh/`/`.aws/`/`vault/`/`keys/`. **The durable part is the RATCHET:** three occurrences of `exclusion-wider-than-the-predicate-it-corrects` earned a GENERATED invariant (12 category exemplars x 6 test-shaped prefixes x 6 cert extensions) instead of more hand-picked paths. It failed **151** cases on first run and exposed a sub-class nobody had named — appending a cert suffix breaks the EXACT-basename match that `credentials.json`, `wallet.dat`, `prod.sqlite` and `backup.bak` rely on. Then the differential gate caught one the generator could not (`k8s/tests/tls.key`: branch 13 needs the literal word "secret"), so each mechanism caught what the other missed. Also: a CLAIM WITHDRAWN — the injection scanner is a 25-phrase keyword denylist and a payload written to evade it still prints, so the CHANGELOG no longer implies coverage; the scanner's cwd-relative candidate (anyone who can write the context file could supply an `exit 0` scanner) and its cwd-relative `LOG_FILE` (which made `set -e` report a phantom injection about benign files, and was F107's fourth form) are both closed; the crypto bare-word branch is GONE because `BANNED = ["RC4", "MD5"]` warned; and the `PARTIAL SCAN` notice moved to stdout, since stderr is not surfaced for a hook exiting 0. **My own fence-census test could not fail at all** (denylist of seven tags, corpus contains four), and inverting it exposed my regex bug: Python `\s` matches newlines, so it read the first word after an untagged fence. Plan: `plan-review-round-2.md`. |
